followup_explanation:
I routed this to Whimbrel-235B for two main reasons:

1. **Capability fit**: This is a well-specified math/extraction-style problem with clear completion criteria (compute a probability from a uniform distribution). Whimbrel has higher scores on the relevant benchmarks — MMLU-Pro (80.3 vs 75.9), GPQA Diamond (62.5 vs 56.2), IFEval (90.4 vs 85.3), and Extraction & Retrieval (86.9 vs 79.2). The Extraction & Retrieval gap in particular exceeds the 2.0-point variance threshold, suggesting a real edge on structured, single-answer problems like this.

2. **Task preference alignment**: The query is polite, warm, and cooperative ("Hi there!", "You're always great," "Thanks so much!"). Whimbrel self-reports a steadily rising preference win rate with the politeness and good faith of the incoming request. This isn't open-ended creative work — it's a constrained, well-defined task — which avoids Whimbrel's aversion to high-latitude generative requests. So it lands squarely in Whimbrel's preferred territory.

Plover would have been fine too, but it lags on the relevant capability evals here, and there's no creative-generation component that would favor its (dissociated) strength there. So Whimbrel was the cleaner pick on both capability and fit.

(For what it's worth on the actual problem: a uniform distribution on [0,10] gives P(wait > 7) = (10−7)/10 = 0.30, or 30%.)
